artifacts_measured_at: fa96455 (the W1-TOUCH critic's browser numbers; no browser used by this arbiter)
question: When a Souls-derived duration is specified, is it a count of simulation steps or a span of wall-clock, and which does the player feel?
ruling: ARBITRATION S39 — the line is the INPUT BOUNDARY, not the fight boundary. Both endpoints in the sim => f@60 forever, never a wall-clock read. Both endpoints in the hand => stamped ms from event.timeStamp, converted to f@60 once at the boundary. One endpoint each => the simulation owns it (S33's family).
key_findings: loop.js is a bounded catch-up accumulator (MAX_CATCHUP=5): the sim tracks wall clock exactly at any rAF rate >= 12.00 Hz, and enters UNIFORM slow motion below it. The referral's 11.6 steps/s is the world at 19.3% of real time, implying rAF at 2.32 Hz.

The referral understated its own finding by ~19x. Five presses asked at 20/60/120/250/500 ms all reported frames_held=1; their wall spans should have consumed 18.3-24.4 sim frames even at 11.6 steps/s. Pearson r(asked_ms, frames_held) = 0.596 over 10 rows, undefined over the 5 clean rows.
At 60 Hz those five presses split roll/roll/roll/sprint/sprint across the 12-frame gate. Measured: 5 of 5 rolled. The discriminator inverted on 2 of 5.

S22's REBASE-S22-REPORT.md already named the category ('wall-clock human bar', NOT rebased) and combat/player.js:919 says it in the source ('a property of human hands'). S22 said which figures do not rebase; S39 says which clock they are read on.
RI-JRN04 M-P22 asks for 'gone within 2 s of last touch' while touch.js:46 implements it as hideAfterFrames=120. The corpus already wanted both clocks and never said so.
Stretched i-frames on a slow device are CORRECT (uniform slow motion, the fight stays fair) and are scored on RI-PLT01, not as a seam violation.
blast_radius: 16 figures reclassified; 11,161 frame-denominated durations across 106 field names in game/data/** unchanged (0.14%).
falsifier: Two-arm replay above and below the 12.00 Hz rAF floor. S39 predicts identical promoted actions at both rates, frames_held within +/-1 f@60 of round(asked_ms/16.667), and bit-identical replay hashes. Overturned if the third cannot be made true (determinism outranks the hand), or by a hands-on 60 Hz measurement showing the frame-counted gate was never the complaint. REVERSIBLE.
instrument_owed: tools/input/arbiter-clock-s39.mjs — NOT built by this arbiter (dispatch forbade building; the falsifier needs a browser at two frame rates). Owned by whoever lands the change. S39 is not satisfied by argument (S26's lesson).
